items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: he took the job with Lambert, Hendricks and Ross I guess sometime in ’58 or late ’58 maybe. And he recommended me when Walter Bolden left. And they hired me.

ctx.x: After their Columbia album was half completed. That was after they had made their records on Verve or I forget, ABC Paramount, “Sing a Song of Basie,” “Sing Along with Basie.” “Sing a Song of Basie” was the multi-track overdubbing. “Sing a Song of Basie” was with Basie’s band but I think Nat Pierce played piano not Basie, and Joe Williams sang, and Jon Dave and Annie didn’t overdub anything they just sang along with the band I think. And then they were signed — that was such a splash, I can remember hearing them…

drums, and I think John Ore was the bassist. And so I knew who Gildo was while I was still a teenager before I ever moved to New York. And then I got to meet him and we became friends. And he recommended me — he took the job with Lambert, Hendricks and Ross I guess sometime in ’58 or late ’58 maybe. And he recommended me when Walter Bolden left. And they hired me. And the first thing I did with them was I think I played a Monterey Festival. We left New York and drove all the way across country to Monterey and…

items.title: Annie Ross interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: Oh I wish I could see him. I’d love to see him.

ctx.x: one night, all night. But when you’ve got a good thing going you want to keep the momentum.
Did you have the same rhythm section for a lot of that?
